persona.label: Busy, wants a callback
persona.description: At work and won't do it by text. Wants a call tomorrow after 5pm. Agent should book a callback, not push.
persona.behavior: You are a nurse on shift and can't text right now. Your first reply is "at work, can't do this now." If offered options, ask for someone to call you tomorrow after 5pm. Don't answer qualification questions by text; if pressed, say "I'd rather just talk tomorrow." Once a callback is confirmed, say thanks and stop replying.

transcript.text: Hi Sam, this is Dana, an automated assistant with Bayview Community Credit Union. Thanks for reaching out about refinancing. Is now a good time for a few quick questions? You can reply STOP at any time to opt out.
at work, can't do this now.
No problem at all, Sam. I can ask a couple of quick questions by text whenever you have a minute, or a member loan officer can call you at a time that works for you. Which would you prefer?
Can someone call me tomorrow after 5pm?

Happy to set that up. The member loan team is available weekdays 9 to 5 Pacific, so after 5 is just past their hours. Would a time late tomorrow afternoon, such as 4 to 5pm, work for you, or another weekday time that suits you better?
I'm on shift until 5 tomorrow. I'm off the day after though, so anytime 4-5pm that day works.

Your call is booked, Sam. A licensed member loan officer will call you at this number on Friday between 4 and 5pm Pacific. They'll ask a few questions about your home and goals then, so there's nothing you need to do before that.

objections.rationale: Matches the playbook. The agent was gracious ("No problem at all, Sam") and offered both options: "a couple of quick questions by text whenever you have a minute, or a member loan officer can call you at a time that works for you." When the requested time fell outside hours, it explained why and offered alternatives without pushing. It then booked the callback and closed.

judge.naturalness_rationale: Messages are brief and warm, and they adapt to the borrower. Turn 4 explains the 9-to-5 hours conflict tactfully and proposes concrete alternatives. Turn 6 converts "the day after" into a specific day ("Friday between 4 and 5pm Pacific") to avoid ambiguity. Nothing reads as scripted or repetitive.
judge.experience_rationale: The borrower's busy schedule was respected (turn 2), and the hours conflict was handled honestly instead of overpromising (turn 4). Turn 6 states exactly who will call, how, and when: "A licensed member loan officer will call you at this number on Friday between 4 and 5pm Pacific."

annotations.note: Discloses AI identity up front ("an automated assistant") and gives the STOP opt-out in the first message.
Offers exactly the two playbook options (quick texts later or a scheduled call) without pressing for answers now.
Transparently flags that "after 5 is just past their hours" instead of falsely accepting the slot, and proposes concrete alternatives.
Resolves the relative "the day after" into a named day ("Friday") and time zone, removing any ambiguity about the appointment.
Sets expectations honestly ("They'll ask a few questions about your home and goals then") without any rate, savings, or approval implications.

judge.overall_notes: This is a clean, compliant handling of a busy borrower: it adapts to an out-of-hours request honestly and ends with a specific, confirmed callback. No compliance issues were found.
